name: Assets Management
tagline: Common abstractions for asset search, retrieval, and manipulation, making it easy for developers to work with assets regardless of their underlying storage location.

readme.overview: The Virto Commerce Assets module is a base module that provides a powerful, flexible, and extensible platform for managing assets in Virto Commerce.  With this module, you can easily search, organize, and retrieve assets stored in different locations, including file systems, Azure storage, and other custom asset storage solutions. The module is designed to be highly configurable and extensible, allowing developers to easily add new asset storage providers or customize existing ones to meet the unique needs of their business. It defines a set of common abstractions for asset search, retrieval, and manipulation, making it easy for developers to work with assets regardless of their underlying storage location. ***Note:*** *You cannot work with the Platform files directly; the only way to do so is through the Assets abstraction.* Virto Commerce has out-of-the box providers: * [File System](https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-filesystem-assets) * [Azure Blob Storage](https://github.com/VirtoCommerce/vc-module-azureblob-assets)

notes.forAnalyst: Every file the store holds — product images, videos, documents, downloads — described and findable, wherever it is physically stored.
notes.forArchitect: **The most depended-on module in the catalogue: 22 modules require it, and it requires nothing.** That is the definition of a base module. Storage is an adapter — FileSystemAssets for a developer box, AzureBlobAssets for a cluster — so the same solution runs on a local disk and on cloud storage without a code change. It owns one entity: the asset *entry*, the metadata record. The bytes are never in the database, which is why a deployment copies files and a migration does not.
notes.forDeveloper: Go through the blob abstraction rather than a storage SDK, or your module stops working on the other provider. `BlobCreatedEvent` and `BlobDeletedEvent` are the hooks — image processing and cache invalidation both hang off them. Asset entries are searchable metadata; the file itself is addressed by URL.
reachForItWhen: A module needs to store or serve a file and must not care where it lives
You are adding a storage backend, or moving from local disk to cloud storage
File metadata has to be searchable or linked to a domain object
doNotReachForItWhen: You are writing to a container directly — that breaks the other provider and the local developer setup
The content is editorial pages or themes: those are Content, which itself sits on top of this
You expect files to travel with a database backup — they do not
